article: Influence of Print Speed on the Mechanical Performance of 3D-Printed Bio-Polymer Polylactic Acid

evidence_classes.process_group_means_and_standard_deviati: Figure 6/9/12 plotted mean and mean +/- one SD
evidence_classes.postpeak: Figure 8 representative colored curves, rescaled by <=2% to the corresponding measured group mean
evidence_classes.prepeak: cubic reconstruction constrained by plotted mean modulus, mean strength, and digitized peak strain
evidence_classes.fracture_drop: assumed zero-stress drop one image pixel after the visible curve endpoint

limitations: The five raw tensile curves for each group are not available.
Figure 8 is representative/aggregated and is not identified as a raw individual-specimen trace.
The reconstructed pre-peak branch is not a measured plastic law.
The terminal zero-stress point is a numerical fracture assumption, not a measured traction-separation law.
Apparent tensile energy density is not fracture energy.
X/Y are build-plate axes; the layer path remains oriented the same way relative to the specimen.
The process profiles are for solid rectilinear tensile coupons on an A1 mini and are not universal constants for sparse infill.
